title: Gemini Notebook made your study notes into something you can explore
content_html:
Published Nov 17, 2026, 12:17 AM EST

I've been writing about Android since 2011, with a focus on device reviews, Samsung and Google Pixel hardware, and the latest happenings in the ecosystem. In my entire writing career, I've reviewed more than 75 Android phones.

Carrying both a Samsung or Pixel flagship and an iPhone as a daily driver provides me with deep insight into how Android works and how it compares to iOS.

I have been writing for Android Police since 2021, covering news, how-tos, and features. You can find my previous work on Neowin, AndroidBeat, Times of India, iPhoneHacks, MySmartPrice, and MakeUseOf.

When not working, I tend to mindlessly scroll through X, play with new AI models, or go on long road trips. You can reach out to me on X or drop a mail at rajesh@androidpolice.com.

Gemini Notebook already makes it easy to sort through your detailed notes and research topics. But now, with its latest feature, it is upping the game and giving you an even more interactive way to view and explore that information. Gemini Notebook can now turn your sources into interactive websites, so you can build visual study guides, dashboards, or project trackers, all with a single prompt.

In an existing project in Gemini Notebook, you can build an interactive website by typing "make me a site" followed by the description of what you want. The tool will automatically use your sources and pull relevant information from them to build an interactive website around that. The company was spotted testing this feature in August this year.

In its announcement, Google says you can use this feature in the following ways:

  • Visual explainers to help you prepare for exams, like an interactive periodic table or a historical timeline.
  • Interactive dashboards to explore your data, such as quarterly sales performance.
  • Project management trackers to outline your tasks and deadlines.

Once Gemini Notebook has built the site, you can use the "Open in a new tab" option to interact with it.

The main highlight of this feature is that you get a different way to work through your already collected information. An interactive website can be especially useful for understanding complex topics, comparing figures, or when you want to visualize your data for better understanding.

For example, you can create a historical timeline on an interactive website to understand the sequence of events better. This is any day better than going through several pages of notes.

As always, make sure to give a detailed prompt to Gemini Notebook when building an interactive website, clearly describing what you want, to understand who the site is for and the different ways you want to explore the information.

The best part is that you can share the generated interactive website with others. So, you can collaborate with your study group or friends when trying to understand a complex topic.

For now, the ability to build interactive websites using your existing sources is rolling out to Gemini Notebook users globally on the web. Google says the feature will soon expand to the mobile app.

Gemini Notebook keeps getting better

Interactive websites are one of the many useful features that Google has rolled out to Gemini Notebook over the last couple of months. Other useful feature additions include 60-second short video overviews and interactive learning overviews, which combine summaries, quizzes, flashcards, and other study materials.

Google has also expanded quizzes with short-answer, multi-select, and fill-in-the-blank questions.

More recently, Google added controls that let you review and adjust slide and video plans before generating them. Plus, it made hundreds of textbooks from providers in the US and India available for free to students, giving them more study materials to build their sources around.
